title: Build a filter from scratch
idea: TOOL: assemble a filter token by token and line by line, for a real framing. More hands-on building, still predicting output.

exercises.prompt: You want to keep only the donations of 100 or more from donations = [50, 120, 30, 200]. What should the first line be?
exercises.explanation: Start with an empty list to collect the matches. big = donations would just copy everything, not filter.

exercises.prompt:
Build the loop header that walks each donation.

Target line: for d in donations:
exercises.explanation: for d in donations: gives you one donation at a time, called d, to test inside the loop.

exercises.prompt:
Build the test that passes donations of 100 or more.

Target line: if d >= 100 :
exercises.explanation: '100 or more' is >= 100. This if decides which donations get appended.
append adds the passing donation to the end of big. It sits inside the if, so only matches are kept.

exercises.prompt: With donations = [50, 120, 30, 200], what will print(big) show after the filter?
exercises.explanation: 120 and 200 are 100 or more, so they are kept in order: [120, 200].
Data, empty list, loop, test, append inside the if, print. You just built a full filter from its parts.

exercises.prompt: You now want to keep only the SMALL donations (under 100). What is the only line you change?
exercises.explanation: Only the test decides what is kept. Change it to d < 100 and the same shape now collects the small donations.

exercises.prompt: After changing the test to d < 100, what will print(big) show for [50, 120, 30, 200]?
exercises.explanation: Now the passers are the donations below 100: 50 and 30, in order, so [50, 30].

exercises.prompt: Building a filter is always the same four moves: empty list, loop, test, append the passers.
exercises.explanation: Once you know those four moves, you can write a filter for anything. Only the test changes from problem to problem.

exercises.prompt: You want to show HOW MANY big donations there were. What do you add after the filter?
exercises.explanation: len(big) counts the items the filter kept. Chaining a known tool onto your filtered list answers the follow-up question.
